newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl prepared to meet SPD leaders on tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Kohl prepared to meet SPD leaders on tax reform.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Monday he would be prepared for a fresh meeting between coalition and opposition Social Democratic Party (SPD) leaders on tax reform.
Kohl told journalists that if SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine insisted on a meeting, Kohl would take part.
Detailed work on the tax reform plan could only take place in the smaller working group that the coalition and SPD set up after the "tax summit" in February, he said.
Kohl prepared to meet SPD leaders on tax reform
Finance Minister Theo Waigel's planned comprehensive tax reform includes a net 30 billion marks in tax cuts, aimed at stimulating economic growth, investment and jobs.

The SPD favours large parts of the plan, though it differs with the government on some details. It has also said it wants the tax reform to be implemented sooner than the originally planned 1999 launch date.

Kohl met Lafontaine with other coalition and SPD leaders in late February. A second meeting of a smaller "working group" was also held, but a scheduled third meeting was canceled by the SPD in protest at the government's plan to cut subsidies for coal miners.

Since then, Kohl has been rebuffing Lafontaine's call for another top-level meeting. The government hopes to win a consensus with the opposition to ease the reform's passage through the upper house of parliament, where the SPD holds a majority.
